Estimate NSEC values from a fitted model

Source: R/nsec.R
nsec.Rd

Estimates the No-Significant-Effect Concentration (NSEC), the concentration at which the fitted response departs from the control by more than its uncertainty allows, in each direction, for a fitted concentration-response model.

Usage

nsec(
  object,
  ...,
  sig_val = 0.01,
  type = "absolute",
  anchor = NULL,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL,
  draws = FALSE,
  prob_vals = c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975),
  xform = identity,
  posterior = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  hormesis_def = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  horme = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  by_group = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  curveid = lifecycle::deprecated()
)

Arguments

object

A model fitted with brms, drc or bayesnec, or a toxval_pred object.

...

Additional arguments passed to toxval_predict(), such as n_boot and seed for a drc fit, or asymptote for a brmsfit.

sig_val

A number strictly between 0 and 0.5, the quantile of the control realisations that sets the decreasing reference; 1 - sig_val sets the increasing one.

type

One of "absolute", "relative" or "range", naming the span ecnsec is a proportion of. See ecx().

anchor

For a model-averaged fit, the control the reference is taken from: "model" uses the control of the averaged model, and "component" uses the control of each component model over every draw of its fit. The default is "component" for a bayesmanecfit, matching bayesnec::nsec(), and "model" otherwise. Both give the same result for a single model. Under "component" the reference column reports the prob_vals[1] quantile of the component references across realisations, as control does.

x_var

A string naming the predictor variable in object, or NULL where the class of object records which of its variables is the predictor. Each method states whether it accepts NULL.

group_var

A string naming the grouping variable in object, or NULL for a single curve.

resolution

A whole number giving the number of predictor values to evaluate the curve at. Larger values estimate a metric more precisely.

x_range

A numeric vector of length 2 giving the range of predictor values to evaluate over, or NULL to use the range in the model data. The first value must equal the control concentration.

x_control

A number, the control concentration, at which the control response is predicted and the grid starts, or NULL for the lowest predictor value in the data. A value outside the range of the data warns.

draws

A flag. If TRUE, a draws list column holds the per-realisation values of each row.

prob_vals

A numeric vector of the central, lower and upper quantiles to summarise the realisations by, in that order.

xform

A function applied to the per-realisation concentrations before they are summarised, such as exp for a model fitted on log concentration. It must be monotone over the evaluated range and may be decreasing.

posterior

Supplying it is an error. Use draws.

hormesis_def, horme

Both directions are now always estimated, so these are ignored.

by_group

Supplying group_var gives one estimate per level.

curveid

Use group_var.

Value

A toxval tibble with one row per curve and direction, and the columns:

  • metric: "nsec".

  • direction: "decreasing" or "increasing".

  • group: the level of group_var, where it is supplied.

  • response: the response of a multivariate fit.

  • estimate, conf.low, conf.high: the NSEC, as the prob_vals quantiles of the realisations, after xform.

  • sig_val, type, anchor: the arguments of the call.

  • control: the predicted response at the control concentration.

  • reference: the sig_val (decreasing) or 1 - sig_val (increasing) quantile of the control realisations, whose crossing is the NSEC.

  • asymptote: the asymptote ecnsec is measured to, or NA unless type is "relative".

  • ecnsec, ecnsec.low, ecnsec.high: the effect at the NSEC, as a proportion of the span named by type, summarised by prob_vals.

  • draws: where draws = TRUE, a tibble per row of .draw, value.draw, the NSEC of each realisation after xform, and ecnsec.draw. A realisation that does not reach the reference is Inf in value.draw, or -Inf where xform is decreasing, and one excluded from the summary is NA.

control, reference and asymptote are on the response scale, as the central prob_vals quantile of the realisations. The tibble prints the model class and the number of realisations above the rows.

Details

The model is evaluated over a grid of concentrations once per realisation, by toxval_predict(): once per posterior draw for a Bayesian fit, and once per parametric bootstrap replicate for a frequentist one.

The reference for the decreasing direction is the sig_val quantile of the control realisations, the predicted response at the control concentration (by default the lowest concentration in the data; see toxval_predict()), and for the increasing direction the 1 - sig_val quantile. The NSEC is found for each realisation against that reference, and the realisations are summarised by prob_vals. A direction in which no realisation crosses is returned with NA estimates.

By construction, about sig_val of the realisations have a control already past the reference. These are placed at the control concentration, unless they show no effect in the tested range. A realisation that does not reach the reference within the evaluated range ranks above the highest concentration, and an interval limit that falls among such realisations is reported as the highest concentration, with a warning. When any realisation is censored, the reported quantiles are observed order statistics.

ecnsec is the effect at the NSEC, as a proportion of the span named by type: the inverse of the ecx() reference under the same type.

NSECs are not estimated for drc NEC models, whose threshold is a parameter of the model rather than a feature of a smooth curve.

Fits from bayesnec

nsec() also accepts a bayesnecfit or bayesmanecfit from bayesnec::bnec() when bayesnec is installed. bayesnec has its own nsec(), and when both packages are loaded with library(), the one loaded last is used. Call toxval::nsec() to make sure this function runs.

The two functions can give different estimates for the same fit, because they evaluate the curve at different concentrations and handle realisations that never reach the reference differently.

Multivariate fits

A multivariate fit gives rows for each response, named in the response column. This replaces nsec_multi(), whose help page shows how to convert existing calls.

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- drc::drm(rootl ~ conc, data = drc::ryegrass, fct = drc::LL.4())
nsec(fit, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high sig_val type     anchor control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>
#> 1 nsec   decreasing     1.18    0.637      1.52    0.01 absolute model     7.80
#> 2 nsec   increasing    NA      NA         NA       0.01 absolute model     7.80
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>, ecnsec <dbl>,
#> #   ecnsec.low <dbl>, ecnsec.high <dbl>

nsec(fit, sig_val = 0.05, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high sig_val type     anchor control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>
#> 1 nsec   decreasing     1.03        0      1.41    0.05 absolute model     7.80
#> 2 nsec   increasing    NA          NA     NA       0.05 absolute model     7.80
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>, ecnsec <dbl>,
#> #   ecnsec.low <dbl>, ecnsec.high <dbl>

nsec(fit, type = "range", seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high sig_val type  anchor control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr> <chr>    <dbl>
#> 1 nsec   decreasing     1.18    0.637      1.52    0.01 range model     7.80
#> 2 nsec   increasing    NA      NA         NA       0.01 range model     7.80
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>, ecnsec <dbl>,
#> #   ecnsec.low <dbl>, ecnsec.high <dbl>

# 80% interval
nsec(fit, prob_vals = c(0.5, 0.1, 0.9), seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high sig_val type     anchor control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>
#> 1 nsec   decreasing     1.18    0.881      1.40    0.01 absolute model     7.80
#> 2 nsec   increasing    NA      NA         NA       0.01 absolute model     7.80
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>, ecnsec <dbl>,
#> #   ecnsec.low <dbl>, ecnsec.high <dbl>

res <- nsec(fit, draws = TRUE, seed = 42)
res$draws[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 1,000 × 3
#>    .draw value.draw ecnsec.draw
#>    <int>      <dbl>       <dbl>
#>  1     1      1.42      0.0489 
#>  2     2      1.40      0.0818 
#>  3     3      1.70      0.0635 
#>  4     4      1.03      0.0642 
#>  5     5      0        -0.00139
#>  6     6      1.23      0.0509 
#>  7     7      1.19      0.0308 
#>  8     8      1.36      0.0590 
#>  9     9      1.26      0.0549 
#> 10    10      0.530     0.00787
#> # ℹ 990 more rows

fit_group <- drc::drm(
  DryMatter ~ Dose,
  curveid = Herbicide,
  data = drc::S.alba,
  fct = drc::LL.4()
)
nsec(fit_group, group_var = "Herbicide", seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 15
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  group      estimate conf.low conf.high sig_val type   anchor
#>   <chr>  <chr>      <fct>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>  <chr> 
#> 1 nsec   decreasing Bentazone      17.8    11.2       21.9    0.01 absol… model 
#> 2 nsec   increasing Bentazone      NA      NA         NA      0.01 absol… model 
#> 3 nsec   decreasing Glyphosate     24.4     7.60      34.6    0.01 absol… model 
#> 4 nsec   increasing Glyphosate     NA      NA         NA      0.01 absol… model 
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: control <dbl>, reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>,
#> #   ecnsec <dbl>, ecnsec.low <dbl>, ecnsec.high <dbl>
# }
